chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Shake hands, for it removes the grudges (or enmity).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of shaking hands in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the handshake (*tasafuh*) as a specific prophetic tradition that actively dissolves *sakimah* (the lingering resentment or 'sting' of the heart), thereby transforming mere social interaction into a mechanism for spiritual purification. This practice is deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a recommended act (*mustahabb*) that reinforces brotherhood (*ukhuwwah*) and preempts the accumulation of hidden animosity, ensuring that relationships remain free from the corrosive effects of unexpressed grievances.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Shake hands, (surely) it would remove with the grudges’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Do shake hands, it removes jealousy.”
